A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PKU-SafeRLHF research. All 32 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison despite the changed title.

before.justification: v1 reports original moderation experiments, RLHF comparisons, human/model evaluation analyses, and annotation-agreement results in Tables 1–3 and 8 and associated figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the moderation and RLHF evaluations and the appendix annotation-agreement results.

M1.justification: The data-generation and annotation pipeline, severity-sensitive moderation, reward/cost models, and RLHF/PPO-Lagrange procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendices B–D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PKU-SafeRLHF, BeaverTails, and Alpaca training data and retain the same moderation, preference-alignment, and human/model evaluation tasks. Coverage of 19 harm categories and three severity levels is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Llama-Guard, Llama-Guard 2, Perspective API, and OpenAI Moderation API. Tables 2–3 retain the same RLHF and SafeRLHF comparisons, and Figure 6 retains the same evaluated models. The four removed references were not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported metrics, human-evaluation procedures, model configurations, and training settings are unchanged. For example, Table 9 specifies the same 20K dataset size and two epochs for each training configuration.

E4.justification: Both retain the single/dual-preference comparison, harm-category correlation and projection analyses, cost-model calibration, prompt-distribution analysis, annotation agreement, example cases, and training curves. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report seed 42 in Table 9 and a smoothed ±1 standard-deviation band in Figure 6(b). No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Experimental and dataset-analysis results match throughout, including the appendices. Moderation accuracy remains 0.93 in Table 1; Table 3 retains Alpaca2 helpfulness and harmlessness win rates of 90.25% and 86.50%. The plotted findings and Table 8 agreement values are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including the preference probability, harmfulness sign function, reward/cost losses, and PPO/PPO-Lagrange objectives, are unchanged. Neither version adds mathematical assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same dataset and application claims. The new title emphasizes multi-level safety already present in v1; it does not establish a new scientific contribution or broader demonstrated coverage.

C2.justification: Interpretations of preference decoupling, cost-model calibration, and category overlap are retained. Section 5.1 preserves the same limitations concerning dataset scale, incomplete harm coverage, overlapping categories, and imbalance.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D retain the same generation prompts, filtering and annotation instructions, hyperparameters, and hardware information. Tables 5 and 9, the dataset access link, and the stated CC BY-NC 4.0 license are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 deletes the introductory Broad Impact paragraph and its citations to SimPO, ShieldLM, Tree of Attacks, and ChatGLM-RLHF. This removes limited positioning about prior-project adoption and influence; the substantive related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The subtitle changes from 'A Safety Alignment Preference Dataset for Llama Family Models' to 'Towards Multi-Level Safety Alignment for LLMs with Human Preference.' The Broad Impact paragraph is removed, but the remaining prose and section organization are substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Text reflow changes Figure 4's placement and surrounding wrapping and shifts Figure 5 and Table 3 within their pages. All nine figures and nine tables retain their content, captions, and display structure.

improvement.justification: The retitling and removal of the Broad Impact paragraph modestly change emphasis and concision. The experimental evidence, Appendix D reproducibility details, and Section 5.1 limitations remain unchanged. These limited editorial and layout adjustments produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
